Check prerequisites, install Firecracker, fetch kernel and build template rootfs

Usage: coop setup [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -y, --yes
          Skip confirmation prompts (accept all)
      --vcpus <VCPUS>
          Number of vCPUs (overrides config)
      --mem <MEM>
          Memory in MiB (overrides config)
      --rebuild
          Force rebuild of template rootfs
      --profile <PROFILE>
          Install profiles (comma-separated: python,node,c,fuzz,rust,go)
      --extra-packages <EXTRA_PACKAGES>
          Extra apt packages to install (comma-separated)
      --post-install <POST_INSTALL>
          Path to a post-install script to run in the chroot
      --template-size <TEMPLATE_SIZE>
          Template rootfs size in GiB (default: 8)
      --image <IMAGE>
          Named image to build (default: "default") [default: default]
      --guest-user <NAME>
          Guest username to create in the image (default: "ubuntu"). Baked into the image at setup time and immutable for its lifetime — `start`/`shell`/`exec` read it from the image's `template_config.json`. Use this when a workspace's `devcontainer.json` declares a `remoteUser` other than `ubuntu` (e.g. `vscode` for the Microsoft devcontainer base images)
      --builder-timeout <DURATION>
          Duration to wait for setup image build commands before timing out. Accepts seconds by default, or an `s`/`m`/`h` suffix (e.g. `90s`, `30m`, `2h`)
      --workspace <WORKSPACE>
          Workspace directory to scan for `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`. When present (and `--no-devcontainer` is not set), coop offers to apply the file's `features` and `hostRequirements` to this setup
      --devcontainer <PATH>
          Explicit path to a `devcontainer.json` to use (skips discovery)
      --no-devcontainer
          Ignore any discovered `devcontainer.json` (escape hatch for CI)
      --dry-run
          Translate `devcontainer.json` and print the report, then exit before doing any setup work
  -h, --help
          Print help
